You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From dfbc282c2e16cd6044e4181f150dbd1e2224eaa7 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Masatake YAMATO <yamato@redhat.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Oct 2014 11:49:17 +0900
Subject: [PATCH] check multiple parser methods are not defined in a parser

This fixes a bug introduced in be4a2117494ce73750cec3fd3c7cb4a60e722bcf.

The old commit(be4a21) checked only the case that allparser, parser2 and parser_with_gc
were not set but didn't check more than one were set. This patch checks this case, too.

Signed-off-by: Masatake YAMATO <yamato@redhat.com>
---
 parse.c | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/parse.c b/parse.c
index 557228d1d..2ae586ea0 100644
--- a/parse.c
+++ b/parse.c
@@ -969,7 +969,7 @@ extern void initializeParsing (void)
 				accepted = TRUE;
 #endif
 			}
-			else if ((def->parser == NULL)  &&  (def->parser2 == NULL) && (def->parser_with_gc == NULL))
+			else if (((!!def->parser) + (!!def->parser2) + (!!def->parser_with_gc)) != 1)
 				error (FATAL,
 		"%s parser definition must define one and only one parsing routine\n",
 					   def->name);
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by insufficient validation in the parser definition logic, where the previous implementation only checked if none of the parser methods (allparser, parser2, parser_with_gc) were defined, but did not account for the scenario where more than one parser method was defined simultaneously. This led to a situation where multiple parsing routines could be set, violating the requirement that exactly one parsing routine must be defined. The patch corrects this by ensuring that exactly one of the parser methods is defined, thus preventing potential conflicts or undefined behavior during parsing.

Root cause:
The bug was caused by insufficient validation in the parser definition logic, where the previous implementation only checked if none of the parser methods (allparser, parser2, parser_with_gc) were defined, but did not account for the scenario where more than one parser method was defined simultaneously. This led to a situation where multiple parsing routines could be set, violating the requirement that exactly one parsing routine must be defined. The patch corrects this by ensuring that exactly one of the parser methods is defined, thus preventing potential conflicts or undefined behavior during parsing.
